entities.title: The target type names the intent
entities.summary: A DateTime<FixedOffset> converts to Instant or to FixedOffsetDateTime through TryFrom, so the type the caller asks for is the intent.
entities.context: docs/everyday-api.md requires the caller to name the intent: a DateTime<FixedOffset> can be an instant or a wall time at an offset, and nothing may be chosen silently. Other libraries take an intent argument and report intent-required when it is missing.

options.title: An intent argument
options.consequences: Kept at the JSON layer: from_fixed_offset(dt, OffsetIntent).

options.title: One TryFrom impl per target type
options.consequences: Instant::try_from(dt) and FixedOffsetDateTime::try_from(dt); there is no impl that would have to guess, so a missing intent is a compile error rather than an outcome.

entities.decision: Both: the JSON layer takes an OffsetIntent, and the typed values convert with one TryFrom impl per meaning.
entities.rationale: "The target type names the intent" (comment in chrono.rs); Rust's From/TryFrom are the idiomatic conversions, and they make the choice explicit at the call site.

entities.title: No conversion from DateTime<Local>
entities.summary: There is deliberately no From/TryFrom for chrono's DateTime<Local>; the JSON-layer from_local always answers unsupported (local-zone).
entities.context: A DateTime<Local> only means something together with the host's time zone, which a UTV library must never read.
entities.decision: Offer no typed conversion from DateTime<Local>, and a JSON-layer from_local that refuses every value with local-zone and names the explicit alternatives.
entities.rationale: "UTV never interprets anything with the machine's zone" (from_local's documentation); refusing with a code tells the caller why, where a missing function would not.
